items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012

ctx.x: Do you think it gets harder and harder to innovate in the world of jazz?

That’s a good question. Wynton talks about that. Keith Jarrett talks about that. But I still — Joe Williams said this wonderful thing in the interview, he said first you imitate, then you assimilate, then you innovate. And Warren talked about that. He said, you know, I’m not sure I was an innovator. And I even heard a panel discussion at the Institute of Jazz Studies about, like Clifford was a great player, a great player. But he wasn’t an innovator. The innovators are few and far between. They change the sound…
Um hum. Like world music and everything.
